title: Banker's Algorithm Purpose #1
statement: What is the primary objective of Dijkstra's Banker's Algorithm in Operating Systems?

options.text: Deadlock Avoidance by ensuring system remains in a Safe State

explanation: Banker's algorithm tests for safety by simulating the allocation of predetermined maximum possible amounts of resources.

title: Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) #2
statement: What happens in an operating system when a TLB miss occurs?

options.text: A disk I/O interrupt is immediately fired
The CPU enters an infinite kernel halt
The MMU traverses the multi-level page table in main memory to fetch the frame number and updates the TLB
The process is terminated with segmentation fault

explanation: On a TLB miss, page table lookup is performed in RAM. If the page is present in RAM, TLB is updated; if not, a Page Fault is raised.

title: Belady's Anomaly in Page Replacement #3
statement: Belady's Anomaly (increasing page frames increases page faults) can occur in which page replacement algorithm?
explanation: FIFO is not a stack algorithm and can exhibit Belady's Anomaly where allocating more frames results in more page faults.

title: Context Switching Overhead #4
statement: What state components are saved and restored during an OS process context switch?

options.text: Program Counter, CPU Registers, Stack Pointer, and Process Control Block (PCB)

explanation: Context switching preserves CPU register state, PC, and memory management registers within the process's PCB.

title: Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) #94
statement: What happens in an operating system when a TLB miss occurs?

options.text: A disk I/O interrupt is immediately fired
The CPU enters an infinite kernel halt
The MMU traverses the multi-level page table in main memory to fetch the frame number and updates the TLB
The process is terminated with segmentation fault

explanation: On a TLB miss, page table lookup is performed in RAM. If the page is present in RAM, TLB is updated; if not, a Page Fault is raised.

title: Belady's Anomaly in Page Replacement #95
statement: Belady's Anomaly (increasing page frames increases page faults) can occur in which page replacement algorithm?
explanation: FIFO is not a stack algorithm and can exhibit Belady's Anomaly where allocating more frames results in more page faults.
